item.title: 10 tourists killed in fire at Inani resort flagged as risky in June: Fire Service
item.description:
The Tuptup Resort, damaged in a fire at Inani in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, had been operating without any approval from the Fire Service, said Fire Service and Civil Defence Director General Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid.

He said the resort had been identified as “risky” following an inspection in June and served with a notice. However, it continued operating illegally, disregarding the warning.

The director general disclosed the information at a press conference held in the conference room of the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters on Kazi Alauddin Road in Dhaka on Saturday afternoon. The press conference was primarily organised to outline the department’s fire safety preparations for Durga Puja.

A fire broke out at the wooden resort near Patowartek beach in Inani, Ukhiya upazila of Cox’s Bazar, around 7:30am on Saturday. Firefighters brought the blaze under control around 11:30am. By 1:30pm, the Fire Service had confirmed the recovery of 10 bodies from the resort. Six people who suffered burns were receiving treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.

Fire breaks out at Cox’s Bazar resort, 10 dead, 6 victims identified

Fire Service Director General Sultanul Afreen Junaid said the three-storey wooden resort had a restaurant on the ground floor, where food was prepared, while the second and third floors accommodated tourists. However, the establishment did not have a fire safety certificate as required under Fire Service regulations and oversight.

Sultanul Afreen said the Fire Service received information about the fire around 7:30am. The nearest fire station was about 22 kilometres from the scene. Firefighters reached the site promptly after receiving the report, brought the blaze under control and subsequently extinguished it completely.

Asked about the safety and legality of resorts made of wood and other flammable materials at tourist destinations across the country, including Cox’s Bazar, the director general said many had not obtained the necessary permits. The authorities would contact the operators and take steps to bring them under the notice process, he said. Safety messages would also be communicated through the Cox’s Bazar Development Authority and relevant associations.

Warning that the risk of such incidents could increase during the upcoming dry season, the director general said those concerned needed to remain alert.

Regarding the cause of the fire, he said it would be possible to determine the origin after a thorough investigation. He also said the Fire Service would review existing laws, limitations in monitoring and possible courses of action to address cases in which risky establishments continue operating despite receiving notices, and to ensure effective measures against similar resorts nationwide.

Special vehicles planned to reach narrow roads quickly

Speaking about frequent fires, unauthorised factories and warehouses, and the risks posed by explosive materials in Old Dhaka, the director general said narrow roads in densely populated areas and the lack of adequate space between buildings posed major challenges for the Fire Service.

These conditions make it difficult for firefighters to reach incident sites quickly with heavy firefighting vehicles and equipment, he said.

He stressed the importance of complying with building codes and relevant regulations during construction. Ensuring all safety measures in old residential areas overnight would be difficult and time-consuming, he said.

Despite repeated efforts to raise awareness about compliance with regulations for new buildings, many people continued to disregard them.

Outlining alternative plans to overcome these limitations and improve response capacity, the director general said the department was planning to use specialised three-wheeled vehicles to reach congested areas and narrow roads quickly.

The department was also considering whether firefighters could carry hoses on motorcycles, connect them to water reservoirs in nearby buildings and use the water to extinguish fires immediately, he added.

item.title: "My 3 sisters lost 5 children, they came to visit in a group of 9"
item.description:
"Six of my nephews and nieces have died. I have three sisters. I am the only brother. Five of my three sisters' children died. The eldest niece's child also died. They had come for a vacation in a group of nine. Three survived," Aminul Islam lamented.

He is a resident of the capital city Dhaka.

On Saturday morning, around 7: 30AM, a fire at the wooden Tuptup Resort on the Patuartek beach of Inani in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar, claimed the lives of six of his family members. On hearing the news, he flew from Dhaka to Cox's Bazar.

At around 2 PM today, Aminul Islam shared this information with journalists at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.

He said, "They were supposed to return to Dhaka around 10:30 AM today. They came to Cox’s Bazar for a vacation last Thursday. When the fire broke out in the morning, two of them were outside. They informed me of the incident."

The resort where the fire broke out at Inani in Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, is named Tuptup. At 2:15PM today, Cox’s Bazar Fire Service Deputy Assistant Director Syed Morshed Hossain confirmed to Prothom Alo that ten bodies were recovered in the incident.

He mentioned that there could be more bodies. The rescue operation is ongoing.

According to local sources, the fire started at the resort adjacent to Marine Drive road at around 7: 30 AM. On receiving the news, the fire service personnel reached the scene. Later, local residents, with police assistance, began controlling and rescue operations.

Fire Service and Civil Defence Chattogram Division’s Deputy Director Md Toufikul Islam Bhuiyan said that Cox’s Bazar Fire Service was notified of the fire at 7: 23 AM today.

The fire service team arrived at the site around 8 AM. The fire was brought under control at 8: 15 AM. Four people died in the two toilets on the third floor.

Toufikul Islam Bhuiyan stated that strong winds from the sea quickly spread the fire in the wooden resort.

Such establishments need to have portable fire extinguishers, fire alarms, hoses, and fire safety plans. But none of these were present in the resort. There was no fire licence either. The resort had been built only seven or eight months ago.

He also mentioned that there was a dispute over the ownership of the place.

Among the deceased, identities of six have been confirmed—Dhaka's Ishrat Jahan Maliha (30), Milita Mehezabin Alvi (23), Laila Jahan Nabila (27), Nafishta Mim (27), Chuadanga’s Fariha Kabir (33), and five-year-old Faizan Ahmed.

Among the six identified, five are women and one is a child.

Six burn victims from the incident are being treated at Cox's Bazar Sadar Hospital.

Among them are Mugda Medical College Hospital’s doctor Shihab Uddin (31) and his wife Nafiza Nawaz Khan (29).

item.title: Being ‘arrogant’ without actually being arrogant
item.description:
There comes a point in almost everyone’s life when he or she discovers an uncomfortable truth: Being nice to everyone is not necessarily a sign of good character. Sometimes it is unnecessary courtesy and benevolence shown to the wrong people. And sometimes the recipient considers your politeness as sheer weakness.

However, this reality is seemingly pre-dominant in most of our workplaces particularly, in a newspaper office. Given my significant experience in the English print media journalism, I found that most of the time I had been and still am surrounded by three types of people : Those who produce the newspaper, those who discuss how the newspaper should be produced, and those who somehow manage to do neither while unrelentingly voicing strong opinions about everyone else's performance.

Let us assume our character to be Mr F.

Mr F is the editorial chief of a respected English-language newspaper. He is professional, experienced and, disturbing for his enemies since he is good at his job. He could take a chaotic pile of news reports, political statements, and press releases badly and wildly translated copies and turn them into a coherent article before the one and only serving of muri-chanachur reaches his table. Penning an editorial is usually a piece of cake for him. He also mingles freely with everyone. This, as he eventually discovers, is his first mistake.

He believes in the old-fashioned Bengali virtues: Respect your elders, listen to people, don't unnecessarily hurt anyone's feelings, offer tea, help the junior colleague, answer the message, and return the phone call. In other words, Mr F behaves as if civilisation in this part of the world is still functioning.

However, his colleagues are often equipped with other ideas.
There is Mr X, whose key professional achievement has been to survive in the same position for 35 years. There is Ms Y, who had perfected the technique of looking extremely busy while producing remarkably little. And there is Mr Z, who had never written a memorable headline in his life but somehow had developed a PhD-level expertise in explaining why everybody else's headline is always wrong.

They may not be incompetent in the dramatic sense. But they are something even more interesting: Comfortably Mediocre. They had climbed-up that beautiful professional hilltop (Please read the newspaper office) where ambition had died long ago, but resentment remained surprisingly fit.

Mr F's success therefore presented them with a daily existential threat. He isn't rude to them. No point competing with them. He isn't even particularly interested in them. This is surely intolerable, since nothing annoys a mediocre person quite like discovering that the person they dislike continuously ignores them.

So the small manipulative moves began to turn Mr F reactive. A crude remark said every now and then. Insults are hurled through a third party, so that it reaches Mr F through another colleague and then via another one. Mr F uses designer brand perfume kept free for all on top of his desk, but his foes compare the fragrance often with a corpse surrounded by incensed sticks. Or a meeting where Mr F's advice was carefully and collectively ignored and then, five minutes later repeated and endorsed by the editor to great applause.

At times it seems like a silent whisper in the corridor or a raised eyebrow. A typical “Ami kichhu bolini, but…” followed by an entire indictment of the man's character. And then comes the classic workplace accusation: F has become arrogant.

This surely puzzles Mr F. He has not become arrogant. He has simply become tired. Here comes the crucial distinction between becoming arrogant without knowledge and authority and becoming arrogant in an artful way.

Blind arrogance says, “I am superior to you.” Artful arrogance says, “I have more important things to do.”

Unfortunately, to people accustomed to having access to your attention, the second can look exactly like the first. This is where many good people get into trouble. They think if they stop explaining themselves, people will misunderstand them.

They are correct. People will misunderstand them anyway. Mr F slowly discovers that some people do not interpret generosity as generosity. They interpret it as availability. Some do not interpret politeness as kindness. They interpret it as a flaw as well.

And some do not interpret silence as dignity. They interpret it as an invitation to continue talking about you. You are most welcome to either agree or disagree; this is where a little constructive arrogance becomes useful.

It is not the “Do you know who I am?” type. That sort of arrogance is usually found in people whose CV requires several pages to explain who they are.
However, Mr F''s carefully crafted stoic arrogance says just a “Thank you”, and then doing absolutely nothing.

Someone offers unsolicited advice? “Thank you”. Someone tries to provoke him? His reply is “Interesting”. Someone delivers office gossip? “Oh I see.” Someone attempts to explain why a mediocre decision was actually brilliant? “Fair enough” And now it is time to leave office.

Purely a personal remark - a Dhaka workplace, like the British Empire, was never designed to survive such passive resistance. People wanted emotional reactions. Mr F, however, only gives them punctuation these days. They expected arguments. He offers them either deluxe or single malt, and they refuse it considering it poisonous. They expect arguments, explanations and hyper reactive outbursts.

As he gives his opponents silence, soon the office corridor begins to buzz. “Mr F has isolated himself, what is the strategy behind it.” “He doesn't talk to people anymore.” “He has become very distant.”

This last accusation is particularly amusing since Mr F had spent years mixing with one and all. He had accommodated all the mediocre in the whole bunch in whatever capacity and at least four inexplicable gatherings arranging Biryani. But since he has stopped participating in every little drama, his absence now becomes ''evidence of arrogance''.

This is perhaps one of the established laws of human behaviour among newspaper men: When you stop feeding a particular relationship, the person who was eating and drinking from you will accuse you of starving them. Eventually, the petty manoeuvres become more soap-opera type. For instance, a rumour is carefully planted and then circulated within the office about Mr F’s remaining a bachelor.

A minor editorial error or disagreement is inflated into a question of leadership. Somebody even attempts the conventional office ritual known in South Asia as “Let's see if we can make him look bad without technically saying anything bad.” It is a difficult art. Then again, it requires the delicacy of an astute diplomat coupled with the imagination of a Bengali auntie.
But Mr F had already learnt something by then. He did not need to defeat every accusation. He just needs to keep doing his work. That is his revenge. Not the cinematic kind. No dramatic confrontation. No slammed doors. No speech beginning with “Let me tell you something.”

And here lies the peculiar tragedy of professional mediocrity: People can spend years trying to reduce someone else''s credibility without growing an inch themselves. Mr F hadn't become arrogant because he thinks he is better than everyone.

He now has become selectively unavailable because he finally understands that not everyone deserves equal access to his valuable time, attention, generosity or emotional energy.

And yes, some people will call you arrogant. Let them. If you are polite, they may call you weak. If you are generous, they may call you foolish.
If you are quiet, they may call you a conspirator. If you are successful, they may call you lucky. If you answer them, they may call you reactive. And if you don''t answer them, they may call you arrogant again. At some point, it is important for Mr F to care less about external validation or criticism within the office, since he is mostly surrounded by proven mediocre elements.

The bottom-line however: You do not need to become arrogant. You just need it to become difficult to be misused. Now, there is a difference. You have to be courteous, but don''t need to be permanently available. You have to be generous, but not make your generosity a professional identity.

Respect everyone, but not confuse respect with intimacy. And above all, don't waste your finest emotional energy proving to mediocre people that you are a decent human being. They may already have decided otherwise. So let them.

The British have a wonderfully useful expression for this sort of situation:
“Carry on.” The Bengalis have an equally useful one: “Chhere dao”.
Between the two lies a complete philosophy of survival.

Sometimes you simply smile, straighten your tie, finish the editorial, drink your tea and walk away. Not because I think I am better than everybody else. But because, finally, I have understood that my peace is also a deadline, and some people don't deserve an extension.

* The writer is Senior Assistant Editor, The Daily Observer

* The views expressed here are the writer's own.

item.title: Death sentence for two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia a lesson for us: Shama Obaed
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has described the death sentences of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia as a major lesson for Bangladesh. She made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Saturday afternoon. She also advised Bangladeshis living abroad to abide by the laws of their host countries.

Asked whether Saudi Arabia had informed Bangladesh about the execution of the two Bangladeshis, the state minister said the government had yet to receive any information about the death sentences. However, Bangladesh had written to the Saudi authorities seeking details.

Shama Obaed said a message from the labour wing of Bangladesh’s mission in Saudi Arabia indicated that the two Bangladeshis had been involved in “adultery” inside a mosque in the holy city of Mecca, an act considered a grave offence under Saudi law. The court had taken action under that law, but the Bangladesh government had received no official information. Bangladesh had therefore sent a letter seeking details about the two individuals.

“Based on past experience, I can say that Saudi Arabia has its own legal framework. If someone commits a grave offence under that framework, the accused are punished in accordance with the law,” she said.
“The death sentences of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia are a major lesson for us,” she added.

Shama Obaed said Bangladesh would be able to learn how the bodies could be brought home once Saudi Arabia replied to its letter.

The Saudi Press Agency (SPA), citing the country’s Interior Ministry, confirmed on Wednesday that the two Bangladeshis had been executed. They were identified as Nazrul Islam and Sweety Akhtar.

Gulf News, a Middle East-based news outlet, reported that Saudi security forces had arrested them on allegations of engaging in immoral and indecent acts inside a mosque in Mecca. According to the report, following an initial investigation, specific charges were brought against the two and their cases were sent to court.

The court sentenced them to death under ‘ta''zir,’ a category of discretionary punishment under Sharia law. The report said the judge imposed the sentences considering the desecration of the mosque’s sanctity and the circumstances in which the offences had occurred. The verdict was subsequently upheld by higher judicial authorities, making it final, and a royal order was issued for the executions to be carried out.

Private sources in Saudi Arabia said the trial of the two Bangladeshis had been ongoing at a court in Jeddah for several months. Two prominent Bangladeshi citizens had assisted as interpreters during the proceedings.


Bangladesh and Saudi Arabia are both parties to the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations. Under Article 36 of the convention, when a foreign national is arrested in another country, the detaining country must promptly notify the person’s consulate if the detainee requests it and allow access to consular assistance. It remains unclear whether the two detainees had requested that the Bangladeshi consulate be notified.

A source at the Bangladesh Consulate in Jeddah told Prothom Alo on Friday afternoon that Saudi authorities had not formally informed Bangladesh about the executions before carrying them out. The consulate became aware of the matter only after it was reported in the media. Later on Friday, the consulate in Jeddah sent a letter to the Saudi foreign ministry seeking details of the incident.

Several officials at Bangladesh’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the Saudi authorities would not normally arrest two Bangladeshis and carry out their death sentences so quickly. They also said it was puzzling that no one acting on behalf of the two detainees had contacted the Bangladeshi mission.

item.title: Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport launches artisan bread brand Dhaka’s Best Bread
item.description:
Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport has launched its artisan bakery brand, Dhaka’s Best Bread, to mark World Bread Day. Combining time-honoured baking methods, quality ingredients and the expertise of Master Baker and Pâtissier Chef Philip, the collection celebrates craftsmanship and the pleasure of sharing freshly baked bread.

The launch was attended by James Goldman, Deputy High Commissioner and Development Director at the British High Commission in Dhaka, as Chief Guest, and Sakib Ershad, Director of Trade and Investment at the British High Commission, as Guest of Honour.

Chef Philip introduced the collection and marked the occasion with the ceremonial cutting of his signature sourdough, inviting guests to enjoy their first taste.

Chief Guest James Goldman said, “UK is the largest source of foreign direct investment in Bangladesh, bringing expertise, knowledge, and creating vital jobs in the local economy. Prominent British brands like IHG are not simply taking a slice of the market, but forming long-term partnerships that contribute to Bangladesh's economic ambition. I am absolutely delighted to be at the Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport today to celebrate World Bread Day and launch ‘Dhaka’s Best Bread’. It is inspiring to witness the city's hospitality and culinary landscape transforming at such a phenomenal pace, and we are proud that the UK can play a part in this journey.

Speaking at the launch, Ashwani Nayar, Area General Manager for IHG Southwest Asia and Cluster General Manager for Crowne Plaza Dhaka Airport and InterContinental Dhaka, said, “Bread has always been more than a staple. It is something we break, share and gather around, bringing people together across cultures and generations. In Dhaka, that connection carries a special meaning. From the flatbreads and bakarkhani of Old Dhaka to the loaves familiar to generations of families, bread is woven into the city’s food memories. Behind it lies the craft of preparing dough, nurturing the khamir and allowing time to develop flavour. As the city has grown, its tastes have evolved, adding new chapters to this enduring tradition.

"With Dhaka’s Best Bread, we want to celebrate that spirit while bringing our own chapter to the table. Guided by Chef Philip, the collection combines traditional techniques with familiar ingredients and new flavours to discover. Backed by United Terminal’s commitment to quality and the international hospitality heritage of IHG, we continue to create experiences rooted in Dhaka and shaped by global expertise. Our philosophy, ‘Your Bread, Your Way’, recognises that everyone has their own tastes, rituals and ways of enjoying bread. Ultimately, our ambition is simple: to create bread that people love, return for and share. A memorable loaf does more than complete a meal; it brings people to the table.”

Reflecting on the origins of the collection, Chef Philip, Master Baker and Pâtissier, said: “The story of Dhaka’s Best Bread began when we inaugurated the bakery as the hotel opened. At its heart was our ‘mother’ dough, the foundation from which our bread-making journey grew. It needed patience, care and time, qualities that remain at the heart of every loaf we bake. I still remember the aroma of those first loaves coming out of the oven. It filled the bakery, and we looked at one another and thought, ‘We have Dhaka’s best bread.’ It was a moment of pride, but also the beginning of a promise we would have to earn with every bake. Since then, we have nurtured that beginning into a collection with different textures, flavours and personalities. Each of our five varieties offers a distinct experience, with the same care behind every loaf. For me, baking bread is about helping people find a loaf they connect with, something they look forward to bringing home and sharing. That is when our work as bakers becomes part of someone else’s story.”

The five varieties in the collection are: Artisans — a traditionally baked, long-fermented bread with a crisp crust. Multigrain — a loaf combining seeds, oats and local honey. Wellness — a blend featuring chia seeds, oats and quinoa. Savoury — a rustic ciabatta infused with roasted garlic and Mediterranean flavours. Soft Signature — an exceptionally soft, golden bread made with coconut milk and a delicate hint of turmeric.

Available at Connexions, Dhaka’s Best Bread also offers guests the opportunity to personalise their orders to suit their preferences, in keeping with its philosophy, “Your Bread, Your Way”.

item.title: Cox’s Bazar resort fire: 6 family members die, man survives by jumping from first floor
item.description:
Md Ashikul Islam went to Cox’s Bazar to spend a holiday with his family. He was accompanied by his wife, Israt Jahan Maliha, his wife’s younger sister, Laila Jahan Nabila, and other family members.

However, a fire at the resort where they were staying on Saturday morning turned their holiday into a tragedy.

Six members of Ashikul Islam’s family, including his wife, were killed when a fire broke out at a wooden resort on Patuartek Beach in Inani, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar, at around 7:30 am. Ashikul Islam’s younger brother confirmed the information to Prothom Alo. Ten people have died in the incident so far.

Fire breaks out at Cox’s Bazar resort, six bodies recovered, six injured, all victims tourists

A relative of Ashikul Islam, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said Ashikul had jumped from the first floor after the fire broke out and survived. However, six members of his family, including his wife and her sister, had died. The relative said they were on their way to Cox’s Bazar.

Locals said the fire broke out at the resort beside the Marine Drive road at around 7:30 am. Fire service personnel arrived after being alerted. Local residents later began efforts to control the fire and rescue those trapped, with police assistance.

At around 2:15 pm, Cox’s Bazar Fire Service Assistant Director Syed Morshed Hossain confirmed to Prothom Alo that 10 bodies had been recovered. He said there could be more bodies and that the rescue operation was continuing.

Fire breaks out at Cox’s Bazar resort, 10 dead, 6 victims identified

Six of the 10 people killed have been identified. They are Israt Jahan Maliha, 30, of Banasree in Dhaka; Milita Mehezabin Alvi, 23, also of Banasree; Laila Jahan Nabila, 27, and Nafista Mim, 27, of Khilgaon; Fariha Kabir, 33, of Chuadanga; and five-year-old Faizan Ahmed.

Their identities were confirmed by Subaktagin Mahmud Sohel, resident medical officer (RMO) at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.

Six people injured in the fire are receiving treatment at Cox’s Bazar Sadar Hospital.

They are Mugda Medical College Hospital physician Shihab Uddin, 31; his wife, Nafiza Newaz Khan, 29; Mannan, 34; Meherunnesa, 30; Masud, 30; and Samida, 32.

item.title: Bangladesh to field first against Zimbabwe as Litton, Miraz miss match
item.description:
Bangladesh will field first against Zimbabwe in the tri-nation series in Abu Dhabi after Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza won the toss and elected to bat.

The match was set to mark the start of Litton Das’s tenure as Bangladesh’s full-time captain. However, stand-in captain Towhid Hridoy informed at the toss that Litton would miss the match due to a last-minute injury. Mehidy Hasan Miraz is also unavailable due to fever.

Bangladesh’s playing XI comprises Tanzid Hasan, Soumya Sarkar, Najmul Hossain, Towhid Hridoy, Mosaddek Hossain, Nurul Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman and Saif Hassan.

Bangladesh are playing in a tri-nation series for the first time since May 2019, with Afghanistan as the third team in the tournament.

State Minister Ishraque joins anti-drug drive with firearm, faces questions over its use
item.description:
As soon as he got out of the vehicle, Liberation War Affairs State Minister Ishraque Hossain raised a firearm and shouted, “Catch them!” Someone standing beside him was heard saying, “I’ll shoot you dead.”

The state minister’s bodyguards then ran towards several people to catch them. One of the bodyguards also kicked a man.

The incident took place on Saturday afternoon in the Dayaganj Ghuntighar rail-gate area, near Gendaria Railway Station in the capital.

A video of the incident was posted on Ishraque Hossain’s Facebook page. It quickly went viral, sparking discussion. Another video showed the detained individuals being handed over to the police.

The pistol in the state minister’s hand was blurred in the video. However, it was left unobscured in some parts, where it can clearly be seen. The video also shows two other people accompanying the state minister carrying firearms.

Pavel Sikder, former convener of the Dhaka City South unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, was present at the scene with Ishraque Hossain.

He told Prothom Alo that they arrived there between 3:00 pm and 3:30 pm. The state minister had gone there following repeated complaints from local residents. The police had also been informed, but they took time to arrive.

‘Sir, I haven’t done anything’

The video posted on Ishraque Hossain’s Facebook page was titled, “Ishraque in action: Drug den demolished, dealers handed over to police”. It mentioned the date of the incident as Saturday, 17 October 2026, and the location as an area beside the railway tracks in Gendaria.

The video shows the state minister getting out of the vehicle with a firearm in his hand, after which the people accompanying him move towards several individuals standing beside the railway tracks to apprehend them. At that point, several young men are heard saying, “Sir, I haven’t done anything. I’m a poor man, sir.”

State Minister Ishraque then replied, “The police will come, then we’ll talk.”

Ishraque was accompanied by his two personal bodyguards, Tofazzal Hossain and Lavlu, as well as a government bodyguard. The personal bodyguards were also armed, and the government bodyguard can be seen pointing a firearm.

At one point, a bodyguard kicks a young man. When asked who had kicked him, Chhatra Dal leader Pavel Sikder said it was the state minister’s government bodyguard. However, Pavel could not provide the bodyguard’s name. He said government bodyguards take turns performing their duties.

The identity of the person who threatened to shoot in the video could not be confirmed. Pavel Sikder, however, claimed that no shots were fired at the scene.

What the state minister said

The incident involving State Minister Ishraque has raised several questions, including:

First, was the firearm carried by the state minister legally owned?

Second, even if it was legally owned, can a minister conduct an anti-drug operation while displaying a firearm in this manner?

Third, if ministers and state ministers have to conduct operations like this, what is the role of the police?

Fourth, is it acceptable for a state minister to conduct such an operation without addressing the underlying problems in the system?

State Minister Ishraque told Prothom Alo that the firearm he was carrying was legal.

Ishraque was elected as a member of parliament from Dhaka-6. His affidavit submitted to the returning officer during the election did not mention that he owned a firearm.

The state minister said he had acquired the weapon on 11 December 2025, after Sharif Osman Hadi was shot. He said there had been no opportunity to declare it in his nomination papers when he obtained it.

The deadline for submitting nomination papers was 29 December. Ishraque submitted his papers on 28 December 2025.

Article 25 of the Home Ministry’s 2025 policy sets out the conditions for carrying and using legally owned firearms.

Subsection (a) of the article states: “A person may carry or use a firearm registered under their own licence for self-defence. However, a firearm must not be displayed in a manner that may cause fear or annoyance to others.”

Asked about the matter, the state minister said he was an elected representative and that the Dayaganj Ghuntighar area near Gendaria Railway Station fell within his constituency. Drug dealings take place there, and local residents had repeatedly complained to him.

Ishraque said he had informed the police, but no action had been taken. He had therefore been compelled to go there himself.

The state minister said the police had failed to play any effective role. “I have held meetings with the police at least 30 to 40 times. They give different explanations each time. They say they lack manpower and vehicles, among other things. Previously, several police officers were shot and injured while conducting an operation there,” he said.

Ishraque added that the police had yet to recover fully following the July mass uprising. Drug dealers fired at people from a distance, he said, which was why he had a firearm with him.

“I did not fire any shots, nor did I use it to intimidate anyone. Yes, we conducted the operation, and we are building social resistance,” he said.

However, the video clearly shows the state minister pointing his firearm. Children were also present at the scene.

Asked why the police had not taken action despite the state minister’s instructions, Moniruzzaman, officer-in-charge (OC) of Gendaria police station, said they had conducted an operation on 11 October involving 300 police personnel. Members of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) and the Special Response Battalion (SRB) also took part.

Responding to the state minister’s allegations, he said they remained in regular contact with the state minister and kept him informed about their operations and the results.

‘Govt and ministers are there to give instructions’

Ishraque has been seen posting videos on Facebook of himself taking part in various operations, including drives related to cleanliness and efforts to curb rising commodity prices. His Facebook page has four million followers. However, the video of Saturday’s anti-drug operation has since been removed from his page.

Senior Supreme Court lawyer Sharif Bhuiyan told Prothom Alo that the government and ministers were responsible for giving instructions, while the police should take action.

“If a minister has to take to the field with a firearm to conduct an operation, what is the role of the police then?” he asked. The lawyer said the state minister’s display of a firearm in this manner was illegal.

item.title: Ervine, Taylor rescue Zimbabwe after Taskin’s early burst
item.description:
Zimbabwe posted 271-8 in 50 overs after Bangladesh pacer Taskin Ahmed struck three times in the opening four overs of their innings in the tri-nation series in Abu Dhabi on Saturday.

Taskin finished with 3-44 from 10 overs, putting Zimbabwe under early pressure as they slumped to 24-3 inside seven overs. Brian Bennett, Ben Curran and Tadiwanashe Marumani fell to the right-arm pacer, who conceded just 13 runs in his opening four-over spell.

However, Craig Ervine and Brendan Taylor revived Zimbabwe’s innings with a 158-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Both batters scored half-centuries, helping their side recover from the early collapse.

Taylor made 81 off 101 balls before falling to part-time bowler Saif Hassan, who broke the partnership with his second delivery. Taylor attempted a reverse sweep but was caught by Mosaddek Hossain.

Saif struck again in his next over, dismissing Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza for four, leaving Zimbabwe at 182-5 after 38.1 overs.

Ervine continued to anchor the innings but missed out on a century. He scored 93 off 106 balls, including nine fours, before Shoriful Islam had him caught behind by wicketkeeper Nurul Hasan.

Shoriful then dismissed Brad Evans in the same over to finish with 2-47 from 10 overs, including one maiden.

Zimbabwe lost wickets in the closing overs but managed to cross the 250-run mark. Taskin conceded nine runs in his final over, while the lower order helped the team reach 271-8.

Bangladesh now need 272 runs to win.

item.title: Cox’s Bazar resort fire: Dhaka University, Jagannath University students among victims
item.description:
Two of those killed in the resort fire at Patuartek Beach in Inani, Cox’s Bazar, were students at Dhaka University and Jagannath University.

They were Md Nafis Tehami and Laila Jahan Nabila. Nafis was a student in the Chinese Language and Culture programme at Dhaka University’s Institute of Modern Languages. Laila Jahan Nabila was a student of the 2019–20 academic year at the Department of Chemistry in Jagannath University.

A fire broke out at the wooden resort named Tuptup on Patuartek Beach on Saturday morning. According to the Fire Service, the resort had a restaurant on the ground floor and guest accommodation on the two floors above. It had no fire safety measures, and during an inspection in June, the Fire Service had declared the resort “risky”.

Cox's Bazar resort fire: Nur Alam loses wife, son, 4 other relatives

Ten tourists died in the fire at the resort on Saturday morning. Seven of them have been identified, including Nafis Tehami.

In a message expressing grief over his death, Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor ABM Obaidul Islam said that Nafis and several members of his family had died. Such deaths were deeply tragic and painful, he said, adding that the Dhaka University community was mourning the tragic incident.

The vice-chancellor prayed for the souls of those who died and offered his deepest condolences to their bereaved families. Calling for the cause of the fire to be identified and those responsible to receive exemplary punishment without delay, he said Dhaka University would stand by the victims’ families and provide the necessary assistance.

Fire breaks out at Cox’s Bazar resort, 10 dead, 6 victims identified

According to Dhaka University authorities, Nafis Tehami was from South Chunakhali village in Amtali upazila of Barguna district.

Meanwhile, Jagannath University Vice-Chancellor Professor Md Rais Uddin and Treasurer Professor Sabina Sharmin issued messages expressing grief over the death of Laila Jahan Nabila. They prayed for the forgiveness of her soul and expressed their deepest condolences to her bereaved family. They also wished the family patience and mental strength to overcome this irreparable loss.

Three of Laila Jahan Nabila’s sisters were also killed in the fire. They were Faria Kabir, 33; Israt Jahan Maliha, 30; and Milita Mehezabin Alvi, 23. Another victim Faizan Nur, 5, was the son of Nabila’s elder sister Faria, while Nasir Uddin, 25, was her brother. They had all travelled from Dhaka to Cox’s Bazar for a holiday.

item.description:

It was not immediately known whether anyone had been injured or killed in the incident.
Hafizur Rahman, deputy director of Dhaka Fire Service, said 6 fire service units brought the fire under control at around 5:30pm. He said it was not yet known whether anyone had been injured or killed.
The fire is suspected to have originated in the factory's warehouse. All workers left the factory immediately after the fire broke out.

item.title: Dengue: Seven more die in 24 hours, 1,872 hospitalised
item.description:
Seven people have died of dengue and 1,872 have been hospitalised across Bangladesh in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The figures cover the period from 8:00am on Friday to 8:00am on Saturday, the DGHS said in a press release issued on Saturday.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 865 were in Dhaka division, 260 in Chittagong, 233 in Khulna, 199 in Barisal, 176 in Rajshahi, 67 in Mymensingh, 59 in Rangpur and 13 in Sylhet.
Since the beginning of this year, 110,312 people have been hospitalised with dengue across the country. Of them, 104,199 have recovered and been discharged, while 5,771 remain under treatment in hospitals.
The mosquito-borne disease has claimed 342 lives nationwide so far this year, the DGHS added.

item.title: DSCC launches New Market drive to curb dengue, clear footpaths
item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has launched a special drive in the New Market area to intensify cleaning activities and clear footpaths as part of efforts to prevent dengue.
DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam led the drive after inaugurating the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme on Saturday. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inspected cleaning and mosquito-control activities in DSCC areas as part of the government’s weekly “Cleaning Day” programme aimed at preventing dengue.
During a surprise inspection on Saturday morning, the prime minister visited Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, the Green Road Government Staff Quarters and the government residential area in Azimpur.
Speaking to students at Dhanmondi Government Boys’ High School, Tarique Rahman stressed the importance of environmental protection, dengue prevention and maintaining cleanliness. He also encouraged students to plant trees to help reduce environmental pollution.
At the Green Road and Azimpur residential areas, he spoke with residents and urged them to keep their surroundings clean and remove stagnant water to prevent dengue.
He also inspected cleanliness activities along the main roads and surrounding areas and instructed officials to take necessary measures.
Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives State Minister Mir Shahe Alam, Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah Md Saleh, DSCC Administrator Bir Muktijoddha Md Abdus Salam and senior government officials accompanied the prime minister during the inspections.
The DSCC said special cleaning drives were conducted simultaneously in all 75 wards as part of the weekly “Cleaning Day” programme. City corporation cleaners and mosquito-control workers, along with local residents, took part in the campaign. Awareness rallies and microphone announcements were also organised throughout the day in different wards to encourage public participation.

item.title: Parliamentary body to probe Karnaphuli Tunnel’s financial losses
item.description:
A parliamentary standing committee on the Planning Ministry has decided to investigate the implementation of the Karnaphuli Tunnel project and the reasons behind its current financial losses.
The committee took the decision at its second meeting at the National Parliament on Saturday.
The committee discussed the tunnel’s feasibility study, implementation process and financial losses, and decided to hold a detailed discussion on the matter at its next meeting.
It also unanimously agreed to examine the project’s implementation and financial losses through a proper investigation, with the relevant authorities expected to provide the committee with necessary assistance.
The meeting also reviewed delays in development projects under the Planning Ministry and the reasons for extending their implementation periods.
According to the ministry, the implementation periods of 256 projects were extended in the 2025-26 fiscal year.
The ministry attributed the extensions to complications in land acquisition, dependence on imports, difficulties in appointing project directors, inadequate feasibility studies, delays in releasing funds and conflicts between ministries, among other factors.
The committee recommended effective measures by the relevant authorities to address these problems and reduce delays in project implementation.
In line with an earlier decision, the ministry also provided members with a list of 1,153 ongoing projects under its jurisdiction and presented their five-year strategic plans, explaining how the projects are being implemented.
The ministry informed the committee that work was under way to formulate a new policy for appointing project directors.
It expressed hope that the policy, once finalized, would help resolve persistent problems in the appointment process.
The meeting was also informed that efforts are being made to address regional disparities in project implementation and ensure equitable development of rural infrastructure.
Regarding staffing, the ministry said recruitment of 65 officers and employees across different grades is at the final stage against 221 vacant posts.

item.description:
Bank Asia PLC organized a workshop on Business Management and Financial Literacy for Women Entrepreneurs, with the aim of enhancing the business management capabilities and financial knowledge of women entrepreneurs.
Tazkera Ahmed, head of women banking, and Trisha Taklim, head of payroll banking, along with several other officials of the bank attended the program held at Bank Asia Tower Branch, Karwan Bazar, Dhaka recently.
Women entrepreneurs from different business segments participated in the workshop.
The workshop covered various aspects of business management, financial planning, budgeting, cash flow management, savings, banking services and access to financing facilities.
Bank Asia PLC has been undertaking several initiatives to facilitate women entrepreneurs’ access to financial services, strengthen their business management capabilities and encourage greater participation of women in the country’s economic activities.

item.title: bKash wins ‘Fintech Innovation of the Year’ at Bangladesh Fintech Award
item.description:
In recognition of its contribution to digital financial inclusion through innovative technology and solutions, bKash has won awards at the “Bangladesh Fintech Award” for the fourth consecutive time.
In the 4th edition of the award, the country's largest mobile financial service provider emerged as the winner of the ‘Fintech Innovation of the Year’ in the ‘MFS/DFS’ category, while also earning ‘Honourable Mention’ in both the ‘Payment’ and ‘Digital Lending’ categories.
Recently, Bangladesh Fintech Forum honoured organizations demonstrating innovation, impact, and leadership in the financial technology sector.
Azmal Huda, chief product and technology officer of bKash, received the awards on behalf of the company, alongside senior officials of the organization.
bKash’s holistic financial inclusion initiative, ‘The bKash Impact’, won the ‘Fintech Innovation of the Year’ accolade in the MFS/DFS category for bringing low-income and unbanked populations under the umbrella of formal financial services--including savings, loans, payments, remittances.
Additionally, it has received two Honourable Mentions: ‘bKash NFC’ in the Payment category for enabling seamless contactless payments, and ‘bKash Merchant Loan’ in Digital Lending for expanding collateral-free credit to small and micro-entrepreneurs.
This year’s event honoured 13 winners and 8 Honourable Mentions across various categories.

item.title: BLAST calls for swift probe, justice over killing of Netrokona journalist Alif
item.description:
Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust (BLAST) has called for a swift and impartial investigation into the killing of journalist Lutfuzzaman Alif Fakir in Netrokona, demanding justice for those responsible and legislation to protect journalists.
In a statement issued to the media on Saturday, BLAST expressed deep concern over the killing and urged the authorities to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident, identify all those involved and bring them to justice.
According to media reports, Alif, 44, was shot dead by two young men on Thursday night, after leaving a tea shop in the Telnjia area of Durgapur upazila.
He was the Netrokona correspondent for online channel Rupashi Bangla and also ran a Facebook page called “Detective Article”, where he reported on various irregularities and crimes.
Alif had previously been attacked by assailants on November 10, 2025.
In its statement, BLAST stressed the need to ensure a safe environment for journalists to perform their professional duties, including gathering and publishing news.
The organisation also called on the authorities to protect every person's right to life and ensure accountability through impartial investigations into all killings, regardless of the motive, including personal disputes.

item.title: Health minister: Highest-ever grant given for Durga Puja this year

Sakhawat said BNP leaders and activists are also standing beside members of the Hindu community and extending cooperation in celebrating the largest festival of the country’s Hindu community.
He said BNP is a non-communal political party and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman also believes in non-communal values. “Under his leadership, the government is working to take Bangladesh forward by ensuring peaceful coexistence of the people of all faiths,” the minister said.
He said the government has always stood beside the members of the Hindu community and will continue to do so in the future. He said a non-communal Bangladesh will be built by ensuring peaceful coexistence of the people irrespective of religion and caste, mutual respect and communal harmony.
After the meeting, the health minister handed over financial assistance from his personal fund to the presidents and general secretaries of 80 Puja mandaps in Monohardi and Belabo upazilas.

item.title: PPRC launches book on poverty reversals in Bangladesh
item.description:
The Power and Participation Research Centre (PPRC) launched its flagship publication “State of the Real Economy: Dynamics of Reversals and Resilience in Bangladesh” at the CIRDAP Auditorium in Dhaka on Saturday.
The book is co-edited by Hossain Zillur Rahman and Namira Shameem.
Hossain Zillur Rahman said PPRC’s findings matched those of the World Bank on poverty reversal and the growing vulnerability of the middle class.
PPRC’s nationally representative survey showed moderate poverty rose from 18.7% in 2022 to 27.9% in 2025. Extreme poverty rose from 5.6% to 9.35% in the same period.
The expenditure Gini coefficient rose to 0.436, indicating worsening inequality.
Nearly 18% of households, or 31 million people, fall in the “fragile middle” category, living between the poverty line and the median income level. Stagnant incomes, rising expenses and economic shocks leave them at constant risk of slipping into poverty.
Half of all households have at least one chronically ill member who needs recurring spending on medicine and healthcare.
Combining household data with meso and macro trends, PPRC said the economy is not merely hostage to geopolitical shocks but caught in a structural trap of rising poverty, low investment and low growth.
Jean Pesme, Country Director of the World Bank, said: “The overarching challenge facing the economy requires immediate structural transformation across trade, public finance, and energy efficiency. There is a critical urgency to align the labor market and education with private sector needs to restore supply-side confidence and drive job creation.”
Professor Mustafizur Rahman of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD) said: “Income inequality in Bangladesh has more than doubled, and growth is not lifting people out of poverty as fast as it is across the rest of South Asia.”
Md. Fazlul Hoque, Administrator of the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industries (FBCCI), said: “For twenty years, no sector beyond garments has taken off, and our dependence on RMG exports has only grown, from about 73-75% to 84-85%. Degrees no longer guarantee jobs, and Gen Z will not tolerate visiting government offices 30-40 times for a routine permit.”
Farah Kabir, Country Director of ActionAid Bangladesh, said: “Informal workers are struggling with rising food prices and no minimum wage guarantees. As female employment in the RMG sector declines, we need alternative agro-ecology jobs, child care centers, and gender-sensitive investment.”
In his closing remarks, Hossain Zillur Rahman stressed the need to acknowledge the structural trap of household distress, investment stagnation, and unreformed institutions.
He called for a comprehensive transition compact built on five pillars: economic democracy, new growth drivers, quality education, productivity transformation, and governance reforms for speed and results.
Urging an experiential lens to assess the state’s shortcomings, he described hoirani as an all-pervasive phenomenon across the state, institutions, and governance that eats away at people’s energy, initiatives, and dreams.
He said a hoirani-free reality in economic and political governance must be the core focus of structural reforms.

item.title: President stresses market-oriented higher education to curb unemployment
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Saturday urged public and private universities to produce skilled and competent human resources in line with the demands of domestic and international job markets.
He made the call when a delegation led by Southeast University Board of Trustees Chairman Rezaul Karim paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban. The university's Vice-Chancellor, Prof Dr Yusuf Mahbubul Islam, was also present.
The President said the primary objective of public and private universities should be to develop a skilled workforce equipped for employment in the country.
To achieve this goal, he stressed the need to adopt a holistic approach to higher education so that universities can produce graduates capable of meeting the needs of both domestic and international labour markets, ensuring that no one remains unemployed.
He also urged private universities to waive tuition fees for meritorious students from underprivileged backgrounds.
The President observed that various industries, factories, corporate bodies, specialised institutions and even private organisations in Bangladesh had to recruit employees from abroad despite the presence of a large number of unemployed university graduates in the country.
Against this backdrop, he emphasised the need for universities to provide modern, high-quality education in technical, engineering and technology-related fields.
He also advised industrial and corporate organisations to arrange appropriate training programmes to develop a competent and job-ready workforce.
The chairman of the Board of Trustees briefed the President on the university's overall academic activities. He said the university is trying to operate largely as a charitable and non-profit educational institution.
The university provides tuition fee waivers and scholarships worth an average of around Tk 32 crore annually to meritorious students, financially disadvantaged students and those covered by special quotas, he added.
The chairman also invited the President to attend the university's upcoming convocation ceremony.
The President accepted the invitation and assured the delegation of his presence at the event.

item.title: Maha Saptami celebrated at 628 Durga Puja mandaps in Brahmanbaria
item.description:
Maha Saptami, one of the main days of Sharadiya Durga Puja, is being celebrated at 628 mandaps across Brahmanbaria, with devotees offering prayers for their families, the country and the well-being of its people.
The celebrations began amid the sounds of drums, conch shells and bells, accompanied by the chanting of sacred mantras and traditional ululation.
According to Hindu rituals, devotees worshipped Goddess Durga through Shodashopachara, a set of 16 ritual offerings. The ceremonies included the invocation of the goddess, ritual bathing and the offering of garments, flowers, woodbel leaves, food and sandalwood paste. Devotees later offered pushpanjali, or floral prayers, at the feet of the goddess.
At the Kalaisreepra Town Sarbojanin Durga Puja Mandap in Brahmanbaria town, devotees Rakesh Roy, Bithi Saha, Shraboni Chakraborty and Shipra Biswas said they had offered flowers and bel leaves to the goddess and prayed for the well-being of their families.
They also sought blessings for the welfare of the country and its people.
Achintya Chakraborty, a priest at Brahmanbaria Dakshin Kalibari Temple, said the tradition of autumnal Durga Puja was associated with Lord Rama's worship of the goddess before his battle against Ravana. The worship is known as Akal Bodhan, or the untimely invocation of the goddess.
He also referred to the springtime worship performed by King Suratha in the hope of regaining his kingdom, which is known as Basanti Puja.
The priest said devotees had prayed for the fulfilment of their wishes and the well-being of their families, as well as for peace and harmony across the country.
The next major rituals will include Maha Ashtami Puja and Kumari Puja at various mandaps, followed by Sandhi Puja, according to the priest.
Meanwhile, the police administration has taken security measures at all Puja mandaps to ensure peaceful celebrations.

item.title: Theft of approach lights raises security concerns at Cox’s Bazar airport
item.description:
Repeated thefts of electrical cables and critical components from the Category II Precision Approach Lighting System (ALS) at Cox’s Bazar International Airport have raised concerns over aviation security as the airport prepares to launch international flight operations.
The incidents have come under renewed scrutiny ahead of a security audit by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) scheduled for October 26.
The approach lighting system, installed on piles offshore near the confluence of the Bay of Bengal and the Bakkhali River at the northern end of the runway, helps aircraft land safely at night and in foggy or low-visibility conditions.
Repeated thefts from the system have not only caused financial losses but also raised questions about the security of critical aviation infrastructure.
The issue was discussed at a meeting of the National Civil Aviation Security Committee (NCASC) at the headquarters of the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB) on October 7. According to sources, the airport director and the project director raised concerns over repeated thefts from the offshore lighting system and stressed the need to strengthen security.
Attempts to obtain comments from Cox’s Bazar International Airport’s acting director, Md Golam Mortaza Hossain, went unanswered. He briefly answered one call but disconnected it, saying he would speak later. Subsequent calls went unanswered.
Consequently, no official comment could be obtained on the thefts, the extent of the damage or the measures taken to prevent further incidents.
Sheikh Mohammad Ali, officer-in-charge of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Model Police Station, said no general diary or case had been filed at the station over the thefts.
Senior journalist Nurul Islam Helali described the incidents as a possible attempt to undermine the airport’s development as it prepares to achieve international status. He urged the authorities to tighten security, although no evidence establishing a conspiracy was cited.
Aviation experts say approach lighting systems are essential for safe landings, particularly in adverse weather and low-visibility conditions. Damage to any part of the system can complicate flight operations, raising concerns about the protection of critical infrastructure and the airport’s readiness to meet international aviation standards.
Given the system’s offshore location, those familiar with the matter said round-the-clock marine patrols, modern surveillance equipment and coordinated security measures by relevant agencies were needed to prevent further thefts.
Local residents have also voiced concern over the incidents.
Mohammad Sohel, a young resident living near the airport, said the thefts were alarming as the facility was preparing to operate as an international airport. He questioned how the lights could be stolen despite the security arrangements in place.
Sabbir Ahmed, a local businessman, also questioned how thefts could occur at such a sensitive facility despite the presence of security personnel. He called for a thorough investigation to establish how the incidents took place and identify those responsible.
The government has been implementing major infrastructure projects to upgrade Cox’s Bazar Airport to international standards. The work includes runway expansion, construction of the offshore approach lighting system, a new international passenger terminal, taxiways and an apron, as well as the installation of modern navigation and security equipment.
According to the latest revised Development Project Proposal (DPP), the international passenger terminal building project alone is estimated to cost Tk1,039.35 crore. The broader programme to upgrade the airport to international standards involves investment worth several thousand crore taka.

item.title: ‘Cockroach’ party founder released from Indian police custody
item.description:
India’s Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke was released from detention on Saturday, a day after his arrest during a police crackdown on protests against the election authority.
Dipke, 31, was detained on Friday in New Delhi as he headed to join a rally that the CJP protest movement had called in the capital’s central Connaught Place district.
He walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon, waving to the media and giving a thumbs up as he was driven away, an AFP photographer saw.
“Abhijeet Dipke released,” CJP legal affairs chief Ratna Singh said on social media.
Opposition parties and CJP activists have defied a security crackdown, rallying to demand the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner after accusing the poll body of manipulating voter rolls to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling party.
The commission, which oversees voting in the world’s most populous nation, has denied any wrongdoing.
Two other senior CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, were arrested on October 14 after entering Jantar Mantar, a decades-old protest site that police have declared off-limits for demonstrations. They remain in custody.
Members of Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party have long alleged that large numbers of undocumented Muslim migrants from neighboring Bangladesh have fraudulently entered India’s electoral rolls.
Rights groups and critics however say Modi’s government has eroded democratic freedoms during more than a decade in power, citing pressure on journalists, civil society groups and political opponents, allegations the government rejects.

item.title: Iran backs ‘political process’ to resolve Saudi-Houthi conflict
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Saturday that Tehran supports a “political process” to resolve the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis.
The Houthis have repeatedly attacked Saudi targets including energy facilities and Riyadh’s international airport, where 13 people were killed in a major attack last week.
“We support an inclusive and comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve the issue,” Araghchi said in a speech at the Organization of Islamic Cooperation in Baghdad.
Araghchi repeated Iran’s offer to mediate between the two sides. Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh previously said Riyadh has not responded to Iran’s overture.
On Friday, Iran denied having anything to do with the Houthi attacks, after Saudi Arabia accused Tehran of encouraging the group’s escalation.
In his speech, Araghchi also said “either we build security together, or we will endure insecurity together,” adding that Tehran was willing “to cooperate with all its brothers and neighbors to achieve the first option.”
The Houthis and Hezbollah in Lebanon are part of Iran’s “Axis of Resistance” against Israel and the United States, which also includes armed groups in Iraq.

item.title: Saudi Arabia: Houthi attacks threaten Riyadh’s regional leadership
item.description:
As the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthi militia in Yemen continues to escalate, Saudi Arabia’s most important national priorities are increasingly at risk. On Tuesday, the Houthis hit the headquarters of Aramco, the Saudi state-owned oil company in Dhahran. On Wednesday, the Houthis vowed to continue attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities, and on Thursday a cruise missile was intercepted over the Medina region. While it remains unclear who launched it, the mere attempt raises questions about Saudi Arabia’s role as guardian of Islam’s holiest places, the Saudi cities of Mecca and Medina.
Following last weekend’s Houthi attacks that killed more than a dozen people and injured more than 300 at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, tourists and potential investors are keenly aware of the growing uncertainty over travel and security in the kingdom.
Several airlines suspended flights to Riyadh and the airport was expected to remain closed through at least October 17, according to media reports published earlier this week. Saudi Arabia’s Future Investment Initiative, an economic summit that usually draws foreign leaders and key players in business to the country, plans to offer remote participation instead of hosting attendees on site.
“The hostilities between the Houthis and the Saudi government challenge Riyadh’s image of stability and security amid the wider US-Iran war,” said Timothy E Kaldas, deputy director of the Washington-based think tank Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy.
“The attacks on Saudi Arabia also threaten Riyadh’s efforts to diversify the economy,” Kaldas told DW, noting that these ambitions depend on potential tourists viewing the kingdom as a safe destination.
Since the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, Tehran, and later the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen, have been targeting Saudi Arabia, a close ally of the United States. Saudi Arabia also supports the Yemeni government in its fight against the Houthis with airstrikes in Houthi-held areas of Yemen.
A decade ago, Saudi Arabia launched Vision 2030, a sweeping economic and social reform plan, to reduce the kingdom’s reliance on oil and transform its economy and society.
“Saudi Arabia is pursuing a highly nationalist ‘Saudi-First’ policy, aimed at propelling the nation to the global forefront as an aviation power, a hub for artificial intelligence and a major tourism destination,” Simon Wolfgang Fuchs, a professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, told DW.
Fuchs views the Houthi attacks as a significant blow to these ambitions and the financial resources available to pursue them.
Pauline Raabe, a senior analyst at the Berlin-based Middle East Minds think tank, points out that Saudi Arabia urgently needs to find a solution that shields its population from the conflict while limiting the economic damage and reputational costs.
“It is a race against time,” she told DW, even though the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is no new occurrence. Saudi Arabia supported the Yemeni government in its war against the Houthis between 2015 and 2022.
“The conflict has been flaring up again with renewed intensity due to the general situation in the Gulf and is as such actually a tightening of the status quo,” Raabe said.
However, she views Saudi Arabia’s loss of authority as a threat on the horizon. “In the short term, Saudi Arabia is a belligerent [player] in a region ravaged by conflict,” she said.
Fuchs agrees.
“Riyadh remains a key player through its investments, its position as the world’s largest oil exporter and its role as custodian of Islam’s holy sites in Mecca and Medina,” he said, adding that “by virtue of this role, Saudi Arabia can count on allies and call for the formation of alliances.”
In August, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement. While the latter two have since offered intelligence and defense support for Saudi Arabia, they also made clear that they will not put boots on the ground in Yemen. France and the United Kingdom also offered limited defense support for Riyadh. Egypt, the most populous Arab country with a Sunni majority like Saudi Arabia, voiced verbal support.
“Riyadh is prioritizing the symbolic value of these countries, projecting an image of strong ties with regional powers,” Kaldas said.
However, much attention has focused on Saudi Arabia’s failure to secure defense support from the United States, he added. While Saudi Arabia’s closest ally — the US signaled willingness to support Riyadh with intelligence sharing and targeting assistance against the Houthis — Washington has so far stopped short of committing US forces to direct strikes. For Saudi Arabia, the understanding is therefore that the US prioritizes avoiding opening another front in the regional conflict against Iran.

item.title: Asus ROG celebrates 20 years in Bangladesh
item.description:
Asus Republic of Gamers (ROG) marked its 20th anniversary in Dhaka with an event themed “Dare to Innovate.”
The event celebrated ROG’s two-decade journey in gaming.
The event brought together esports players, gaming enthusiasts, technology reviewers, and industry stakeholders to mark the milestone and explore the latest developments in gaming technology.
As part of the celebration, Asus launched five new gaming laptops and announced a nationwide online esports tournament.
The newly launched models are the ROG Zephyrus Duo (GX651), Zephyrus G14 (GU405), Zephyrus G16 (GU606), and ASUS TUF Gaming 16 (FX610).
The ROG Zephyrus Duo was a key highlight of the launch, featuring two 16-inch OLED displays designed to support gaming, multitasking, and content creation.
The dual-screen setup allows users to play games on one display while keeping chats, guides, or other applications open on the second.
It also offers additional screen space for tasks such as video editing and graphic design.
The Zephyrus G14 and G16 combine slim, lightweight designs with performance suited to gaming and other demanding tasks, offering portability for users who need computing power on the move.
The Asus TUF Gaming 16 emphasizes durability and reliable performance for everyday gaming.
Alongside the laptop launches, Asus announced ROG Showdown, an online esports tournament with a total prize pool of Tk100,000.
The competition will be open to players across Bangladesh, providing an opportunity for local gamers to compete and showcase their skills.
Details on registration and match schedules will be announced through Asus and ROG’s official social media channels.
Md Al Fuad, business development manager at Asus, said: "For 20 years, ROG has continued to push the boundaries of gaming innovation. Bangladesh has a passionate and growing gaming community, and we are excited to bring our latest technologies while creating more opportunities for gamers to connect, compete, and grow."
The event also featured live demonstration zones where visitors could try the newly launched ROG and TUF gaming laptops, offering a closer look at their features and performance.

item.title: FSCD DG: All 538 fire stations prepared for emergencies during Durga Puja
item.description:
Fire Service and Civil Defense (FSCD) has taken comprehensive measures to ensure fire safety at Durga Puja venues across the country, with all 538 fire stations ready to respond to emergencies during the festival.
Director General of Fire Service and Civil Defense Brigadier General Sultanul Afreen Junaid disclosed the preparations at a press conference held at the department’s headquarters in Dhaka on Saturday.
He said fire stations would remain on standby throughout the festival, monitoring fire safety at puja mandaps in their respective areas and maintaining round-the-clock communication with local administrations and puja committees.
During inspections, fire service personnel will assess fire risks and advise organizers on measures to address them.
They will also publicize the telephone numbers of nearby fire stations and the 102 hotlines for emergency assistance, he added.
Temporary fire stations operating in different locations will remain on high alert, while officials at divisional, district and zonal levels will stay on standby to inspect puja venues and respond to emergencies.
The director general also said the central control room and all divisional control rooms would operate round the clock. Upon receiving an emergency call, they would direct one or more nearby fire stations to respond immediately.
All divisional and district offices, along with fire stations, will coordinate continuously with local administrations and take necessary decisions and implement measures in line with their directions, he said.
At immersion sites, the department will deploy personnel and volunteers, road rescue equipment and ambulances. Lighting units will also be deployed at night where necessary.
Control rooms will be maintained at the department’s headquarters and divisional and district headquarters to ensure continuous communication with fire stations under their respective jurisdictions.
Calling for greater public awareness, Sultanul Afreen said, “Awareness is protection,” and sought the media’s cooperation in raising awareness about fire safety alongside the department’s own efforts.
